messages:
Kevin Zhang: Quick follow-up on the prefix-cache ownership boundaries we chatted about in the RFC — I'm worried about a correctness window when we switch model variants for a tenant and simultaneously evict shared prefix entries. Specifically, if Variant A writes a prefix to a shared slab and Variant B (incompatible kv layout) starts serving and we evict based on slab-level pressure, a request to Variant B could read an inconsistent prefix. Thoughts?
Maria Lopez: Good callout. The case I keep thinking about is quantization/embedding shape changes that are semantically incompatible. We can't let stale KV be read by a mismatched decoder.
Alex Chen: Two quick approaches: (1) conservative per-prefix generation/version tag that is validated on read, or (2) lease tokens bound to (model_variant, tenant) that must be presented to read. Both add overhead.
Noah Patel: Generation tags seem simpler: attach a 64-bit generation for a prefix key. On model switch, bump tenant+variant generation and invalidate reads where tag != current. Eviction can still reclaim memory, but reads will fail-safe.
Sophia Rivera: How do we store the generation cheaply across the shared slab? Adding a header per entry will increase memory and CPU for every access. We should consider compressed tags or only applying tags to prefixes that are cross-variant sharable.
Kevin Zhang: Agree about selective tagging. Proposal: default-to-shared entries being untagged (fast path) and only create tagged entries when a prefix has been observed by >1 variant or when we detect incompatible layouts. We need a mechanism to detect incompatibilities at admission time.
Alex Chen: Right — detection: admission path knows the serving model signature. If an entry exists and admission sees signature mismatch, it writes a tagged copy or fails admission and forces re-gen. That keeps fast-path untagged.
Maria Lopez: Concern: race between eviction and admission. If admission observes entry exists, decides to accept and then eviction reclaims memory before read, we need read-after-admit guarantees. We currently have an async eviction scanner.
Noah Patel: We can add a short-lived admission lease (in-memory transient) that pins the slab segment during admission -> read completes or fails before eviction can kick in. Lease would be a lightweight increment on a refcount. Eviction respects refcount>0.
Sophia Rivera: That's similar to what we do for KV-prefetch today. Caveat: refcount increases contended atomic ops on hot prefixes. But admission is rare compared to reads.
Kevin Zhang: Let's sketch an interaction diagram in-thread: admission -> check entry -> if incompatible -> create new tagged entry + bump tenant_variant_gen -> acquire admission lease/refcount -> finish write -> release lease. Read path checks tag vs runtime tenant_variant_gen and refcount to ensure entry isn't in eviction transient state.
Alex Chen: Pseudocode snippet I sketched earlier:```proto
message PrefixEntry {
  bytes payload = 1;
  uint64 gen = 2; // 0 = untagged
  uint8 flags = 3;
}
// runtime map: tenant_variant -> uint64 current_gen
```
Noah Patel: On eviction: when reclaiming an entry, if gen != 0 we must also consult a small tombstone table mapping active gens to liveness. If a gen is still current for some tenant_variant, we skip reclaim or demote entry (move to per-tenant quarantine queue). That prevents reclaiming entries while a variant still expects them.
Maria Lopez: Tombstone table is extra memory but small (one entry per active tenant_variant gen) and TTL-based. We could GC old gens after N minutes.
Sophia Rivera: Also add metrics: gen_mismatch_reads, admission_leases, eviction_skips_due_to_gen. That will let us tune GC TTL and how often we create tagged entries.
Kevin Zhang: Operational question: what should be the default policy for cross-variant sharing? Conservative (no sharing across variant families) or aggressive (allow sharing unless detected incompatible)? My vote: start conservative for safety, then relax with telemetry.
Alex Chen: Conservative start makes rollout safer. We can add a try-share flag in the admission request to opt-in per-tenant later.
Noah Patel: Implementation notes: minimal per-entry overhead (8B gen) plus tombstone map. Refcount can be a 32-bit counter in slab header. We should instrument tail latency on reads to ensure the checks are negligible.
Maria Lopez: Action items: Kevin to draft a short RFC appendix that describes generation tags + admission lease plan; Alex to prototype proto changes and microbench slab access; Sophia to add metrics + dashboard plan; Noah to sketch eviction interaction and tombstone GC. I'll volunteer to coordinate testing matrix for variant-incompatible regressions.
Kevin Zhang: Thanks all — I'll put the appendix on today's RFC branch and ping in here when it's up. @ci-bot can you run a quick perf build when Alex pushes the prototype branch? :thumbsup:
ci-bot: build queued for branch "prefix-gen-proto" (job #4521). Logs: http://ci.internal/4521
Alex Chen: pushed branch prefix-gen-proto, added basic microbench harness. Will link results in an hour.
Sophia Rivera: Nice, I'll add the metrics hooks this afternoon.
Noah Patel: One more note — we should consider a fallback where if a read sees a gen mismatch it can synchronously request a safe re-gen from the authoritative model process instead of failing the request, to avoid increased 5xx. That adds latency but improves correctness. We'll trade that in the RFC appendix.
Kevin Zhang: Good point. We'll include sync re-gen vs fail policy choices and recommend sync re-gen for 95th-percentile low-concurrency paths. OK closing for now, will follow up with the appendix link. :rocket:
